Speculaas Biscuits

Served at: St. Nicholas Day

Makes about 24 biscuitsPrep 20 minCook 15 min

Speculaas biscuits are spiced shortcrust cookies traditionally served on St. Nicholas Day, celebrated on December 6th in the Netherlands and Belgium. These aromatic cookies are flavored with a blend of warm spices and often feature intricate designs stamped into the dough, making them a festive treat for the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/2 cups (310 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
  • 1 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground white pepper (optional)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup (200 g) brown sugar, packed
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) milk
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Method

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, nutmeg, white pepper (if using), and salt.
  2. In a separate bowl, cream the softened butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy.
  3. Beat in the egg, milk, and vanilla extract until well combined.
  4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until a smooth dough forms.
  5. Divide the dough into two discs, wrap in plastic wrap, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
  6. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. Roll out the chilled dough on a lightly floured surface to about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thickness.
  8. Cut the dough into desired shapes using cookie cutters or a speculaas mold for traditional patterns.
  9. Place the biscuits on the prepared baking sheets about 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart.
  10. Bake for 12-15 minutes or until the edges are golden brown.
  11. Allow the biscuits to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

Tips

  • For authentic designs, use a wooden speculaas mold to press patterns into the dough before baking.
  • If you prefer a softer biscuit, reduce the baking time slightly.
  • Store the biscuits in an airtight container to keep them crisp and flavorful for up to two weeks.
